findings.conclusion: pg_roles exposes global per-role defaults by joining pg_db_role_setting on role OID and setdatabase=0. setdatabase=0 is not database-specific; setrole=0 is not role-specific. Preserve arrays and distinguish raw OIDs from logical role identity.

New-login initialization loads exact database/role defaults, then role-only, database-only and global defaults according to precedence. SET ROLE changes current role, not the target role startup GUC set. Existing sessions are not retroactively rewritten by ALTER ROLE SET.

Unqualified lookup depends on ordered schemas and USAGE. Missing/inaccessible schemas are ignored in resolved paths. current_setting returns the configured GUC string; current_schemas additionally reveals resolution. pg_catalog and temporary schemas have special behavior, and $user depends on current role. These special explicit forms are excluded from the proposal.

17.6 checks identifier-list syntax rather than requiring schema existence. Micro replay confirms extensions/auth/storage need not exist for these settings to be restored. This does not prove later object resolution when schemas/ACLs differ.

dumpRoles writes CREATE/attribute ALTER statements before a later user-configuration section. dumpUserConfig reads unnest(setconfig) with setdatabase=0. makeAlterConfigCommand emits ALTER ROLE name SET key TO values and treats search_path as a quoted GUC list; runtime statements/array order are preserved below. --no-role-passwords keeps password material out.

pg_dumpall establishes its secure search path after connecting. pg_restore restores archive-controlled search-path state; its command identity stays the independent transport. Role ALTER SET does not act as a session SET in that connection. No pg_restore was run in F2A.
